title: The Weird Circle
paragraphs: A supernatural and mystery anthology built largely from adaptations of classic literature by writers such as Edgar Allan Poe and other authors of Gothic, macabre, and fantastic fiction.

Transcribed New York literary horror/mystery anthology of 78 programs, distributed in syndication rather than as one simultaneous nationwide network schedule. Frozen GRH contains the complete numbered package; #33 and #64 lack dates/numbers in the production catalog but are recoverable from the documented sequence.
GRH documents the program through Transcribed literary-horror anthology package (1943 to 1945).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Ted Jewett (announcer on 78 recordings), Peggy Mayer (writer on 26 recordings), Alan Devitt (performer on 3 recordings), Alfred Shirley (performer on 3 recordings), Burford Hampden (performer on 3 recordings), Walter Vaughn (performer on 3 recordings), and Edwin Jerome (performer on 2 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include supernatural and uncanny forces, death, murder and mortality, Gothic houses, ruins and confinement, ghosts and hauntings, madness, obsession and unstable perception, and curses and fatal objects.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Transcribed syndication model, Classic-literature adaptation culture, Wartime-era escapist horror anthology, and AFM recording ban and The Weird Circle music-free sound.
